findings.description: The grader_versions tally is sorted with a key that splits each grader_version string on '.' and converts digit-only segments to int while leaving others as str. Python 3 cannot compare int with str, so two grade.json files whose grader_version values differ in segment type at the same position (e.g. "1.2" and "1.x", or "2" and "beta") raise TypeError inside sorted(). grade.json is per-run-directory data the report reads without validation, and the header explicitly promises the batch record is 'never fatal'. The surrounding try/except only wraps the open/json.load, not the sort, so a single malformed or hostile grade.json aborts the whole report (and the --json twin) for every suite version.
findings.failure_mode: A run directory with grader_version "1.x" alongside normal "1.2" rows makes ablation-report.py crash with an uncaught TypeError after all analysis has been computed; no report.md or report.json is written, blocking the promotion decision.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a type-stable sort key, e.g. tuple of (0, int(p)) for digit segments and (1, p) otherwise, or sort grader versions as plain strings after the 'n/a' flag. Alternatively wrap the tally sort in the same never-fatal handling and fall back to string order.

findings.description: batch_record builds the run-directory path as os.path.join(<batch dir>, row['arm']) and then os.listdir()s it and opens <dir>/<task>-t<n>/grade.json. The arm value comes straight from runs.jsonl rows; the arm grammar (^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$) is only enforced by ablation-row.sh --validate, which the report does not run, and an absolute arm such as "/tmp/x" makes os.path.join discard the batch dir entirely. The symlink checks guard entries but not the arm segment itself. Impact is bounded: only directories matching <task_id>-t<trial> are considered and only the grader_version string of a grade.json inside them reaches the report, so this is a directory-probe rather than a read of arbitrary content.
findings.failure_mode: A crafted row with arm "../../other-batch" or "/some/path" causes the report to list and open grade.json files outside the batch directory, leaking the existence of directories and their grader_version values into report.md/report.json.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject or skip rows whose arm does not match the suite's arm ids (self.arms) or the arm grammar before building paths; additionally assert the resolved path stays under the batch directory (os.path.commonpath) before listing.

findings.description: The batch-record table interpolates several STATUS.json / manifest values without md_cell(): trials_planned is emitted raw (it is any JSON value from STATUS.json, including a string containing '|', newlines or markdown), and the batch name is wrapped in backticks but not escaped, so a batch id containing a backtick or pipe breaks out of the cell. Elsewhere in the new code (render_decisions, render_exclusions, render_per_arm) the same classes of value go through md_cell. Since report.md is the artifact humans read to decide promotion, a STATUS.json or manifest under attacker control can inject rows or hide columns in the table.
findings.failure_mode: A STATUS.json with trials_planned "3 | green | ... |" or a batch directory named with a pipe produces a malformed or misleading Batch record table in the published report.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass trials_planned and the batch name through md_cell (and coerce trials_planned to int or 'n/a' when it is not a non-bool int), matching the treatment of the other cells.

findings.description: defects_missed accepts any list of non-empty strings from grade.json recall.missed and writes it into the row verbatim; the --validate branch mirrors this. Nothing checks the ids against the task's seeded defect id grammar (d1 … dN), their count, or their length, so an arbitrary-length or non-id string set reaches runs.jsonl and from there the report's defect_vector / budget_matched defect-union logic and the markdown output. Because the report partitions and renders based on these values, a malformed grade.json can carry unexpected content into the decision artifact without any validation layer rejecting it.
findings.failure_mode: A grade.json with recall.missed ["<very long or markdown string>"] is accepted by the row writer and by --validate, and later rendered/consumed by ablation-report.py with no bound or grammar check.
findings.suggested_fix: In both the row writer and the --validate check, constrain each id to the defect id grammar (e.g. test("^d[0-9]+$")), bound the list length to the task's defect count, and dedupe; null the field otherwise as already done for non-string entries.
